factProposals.value: System settings administrators can change: the public site rate limit per hour, how many days submitters' IP addresses are kept, how many days a vendor submission may wait before it is overdue, and the default heat map cell size. Each has a fixed type, range and default.
A setting change applies across the system on the next request: the public site, IP clean-up, vendor review queue and heat maps all read the current value when they run.
Only people holding settings:admin (system administrators), acting with their own key, can change settings; only access:admin can edit, deactivate or reactivate users and define roles.
Besides the built-in roles, the city can define its own roles from the known permissions, for example an inspector role.
Every setting change, user change and role change is in the audit trail with the administrator's user id, the time, and the values before and after.
factProposals.evidence: server/settings.js (changeSetting); server/access.js (updateUser, setUserActive, createRole, updateRole, deleteRole)

factProposals.value: The city's records retention rule for submitter IP addresses and its rule for when a vendor submission is overdue are still not known; both remain placeholder defaults, now adjustable by administrators.

decisions.statement: Define which settings exist, with their types, ranges and defaults, in code, and store only the city's chosen values.
decisions.rationale: Administrators cannot create a setting the system does not use or enter a value it cannot handle; defaults equal the earlier fixed values, so nothing changed until someone changed it.

decisions.statement: Read settings every time they are used instead of caching them.
decisions.rationale: A change must apply across the system immediately; the reads are small.

decisions.statement: Fall back to the default when a stored setting is damaged or out of range, and report it.
decisions.rationale: A bad configuration value must not stop the system working or be used silently.
Settings are shown through the API and recorded in the audit trail; vendor integration credentials will need a separate protected store.

decisions.statement: Remove a user's key when they are deactivated, and require a new key after reactivation.
decisions.rationale: Deactivation must take effect on the next request, and an old key must never come back to life.

limitations.statement: Only four values are settings; others, such as the one-hour rate limit window and upload size limits, are still fixed in code.
Settings, users and roles are managed through the API; there is no administrator page.
The six built-in roles cannot be edited by administrators; the city adds its own roles instead.
